headline: Welcome rain arrives Saturday afternoon and night, heaviest along and east of I-77 including Charlotte, followed by a very warm Monday and then a much cooler, unsettled Thanksgiving week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps Friday evening dry across the region, including Charlotte. Clouds slowly thicken and lower overnight as a storm system organizes off the Southeast coast, with a steady northeast breeze. Lows stay a bit mild, about 5 or more degrees above normal.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday turns cloudier with gusty northeast winds after sunrise and highs near normal, and rain likely arrives in the Charlotte area by mid-afternoon. Rain becomes likely across the eastern half of the area Saturday night and near-certain along and east of I-77, including Charlotte; most places get 0.1–0.33 inch, but half an inch or more is increasingly likely along and east of I-77, a beneficial soaking. Rain tapers off Sunday morning, though low clouds and lingering cool air at the surface could hold temperatures down for part of the day, and Monday turns quite warm, 10 or more degrees above normal, as skies clear and winds blow downhill off the mountains, with only a few light showers possible in the mountains Monday afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A mostly dry cold front Monday night into early Tuesday brings much cooler air, with temperatures near to below normal from Tuesday through the end of the week. Confidence is low from midweek on because of a complex pattern, but there is a weak signal for a storm that could redevelop along the coast, so there is a chance of rain Wednesday through at least the first part of Thanksgiving Day, with timing still unclear. Depending on timing, enough cold air could be in place for a brief period of wintry precipitation in the mountains at the start.

watch_for: Saturday night rain totals along and east of I-77, including Charlotte, where half an inch or more is becoming more likely.
Timing of midweek rain chances heading into Thanksgiving Day.
Possible brief wintry precipitation in the mountains if the midweek storm arrives while cold air is in place.
confidence: Forecasters are growing more confident in beneficial weekend rain and a warm Monday, but confidence is low from midweek through Thanksgiving because models disagree on the details.
